question: How Do I Create a Jump Link to a Section on the Same Page?
metaDescription: Add a Menu Anchor widget with a unique ID above the target section, then link any button or menu item to "#" plus that same ID.
shortAnswer: Elementor's Menu Anchor widget, placed at the top of the section you want to jump to, is given a unique ID in its settings; any button, link, or navigation menu item elsewhere on the page can then link to # followed by that same ID, smoothly scrolling the visitor to that exact anchor point when clicked, the same underlying behavior as a standard HTML anchor link.

bodyHtml:
How Menu Anchors Work

The Menu Anchor widget itself renders as an invisible marker with a specific ID attribute attached to the page's HTML at whatever position it's placed. Any link elsewhere on the page (or even on a different page, appending the anchor after the page URL) pointing to #that-id triggers the browser's native anchor-jump behavior, which Elementor enhances with smooth scrolling by default.

Common Uses

  • A one-page site's navigation menu, jumping between sections like "About," "Services," and "Contact" all on a single long page.
  • A "Jump to pricing" or "See features" button at the top of a landing page, scrolling directly to the relevant section further down.
  • A table of contents for a long article-style page, jumping to specific headings.
  • Linking from a different page, using the format page-url/#anchor-id to land directly on a specific section after navigating there.

Setting This Up

  1. Add a Menu Anchor widget at the top of the target section and give it a unique, descriptive ID.
  2. Link any button, text link, or menu item to # plus that exact ID.
  3. Test the jump, confirming it lands at the correct scroll position, adjusting for any sticky header offset if needed.
